race.name: Belgian Waffle Ride Mexico
race.tagline: The last Waffle of the year: 180 km of Querétaro ranch roads and wine-country gravel, starting at 1,880 m.

vitals.date_specific: 2026: November 21-22 (race day Sunday, November 22; CONFIRMED — belgianwaffleride.bike)
vitals.course_status: 2026 distances published; no route file or climbing figure published; 2027 routes not yet announced
vitals.distance_options: Waffle +180 km (112 mi), Wafer +100 km (62 mi), Wanna +50 km (31 mi); e-bike categories on Wafer and Wanna
vitals.field_size: Capped at 1,000 riders in 2026; 2024 drew well over 550 riders
vitals.registration: 2026 Waffle: $99 early bird to $220 at the expo, plus 16% VAT; 2027 prices not published
vitals.prize_purse: $5,000 USD cash to the Waffle top five men and women in 2026 ($1,250 to each winner); 2027 not published
vitals.aid_stations: Hammer Nutrition aid and hydration stations on course, plus Shimano neutral service, medical stations and sweep vans; locations not published
vitals.cutoff_time: No fixed cutoffs published; riders who miss time at assistance or regroup points must shorten their ride. Route closes at 6:00 pm (2026).

climate.description: The 2025 edition ran in mild weather under clear skies. The 2026 start town sits at 1,880 m and riders are called to the line at 5:30 am.

terrain.surface: The organizer lists fast gravel roads, technical sectors, vineyard landscapes and ranch roads, but publishes no unroad percentage. A 2023 finisher described technical climbs and descents. The Waffle is gravel-bike only; mountain bikes are allowed on the Wafer and Wanna.

gravel_god_rating.score_note: BWR Mexico lands in Tier 2 on a 180 km Waffle at 1,880 m altitude, a destination course and a modest entry fee. It sits below the US BWR stops because it publishes no route or climbing figure, has three editions of history, and its 2027 date is not yet on the organizer's site. The elevation score is provisional until a gain figure is published.

biased_opinion.summary: BWR Mexico closes the Waffle calendar in Querétaro's wine-and-cheese country: a 180 km Waffle from a start town at 1,880 m, for an entry fee that tops out at $220 plus VAT. It has run three times, passed 550 riders in its second year, and its 2025 titles were settled by two seconds for the men and five for the women. What it doesn't publish is the thing you train for: no route file, no climbing figure, and in November 2026 still no named venue for a race less than three weeks out.
strengths: Closes the BWR calendar, with a $5,000 Waffle purse
Waffle entry from $99 to $220 plus VAT
Close racing up front: 2025 decided by seconds
weaknesses: No route file or climbing figure published
2027 date not yet on the organizer's site
International travel for riders from the US
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Go for a season-ending Waffle at altitude at a modest price. Train for 180 km at 1,880 m and bring your own climbing estimate, because the organizer hasn't published one.

final_verdict.one_liner: A season-ending Waffle at 1,880 m, sold without a course profile.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a late-season 180 km race at altitude with a BWR prize list and a modest entry fee. Wait if you plan training around a published route and climbing figure; BWR Mexico hasn't posted either.
final_verdict.alternatives: For the original Waffle, race BWR California. For another Mexican gravel race, look at Gravel Arteaga in Coahuila.

logistics.airport: Fly to Querétaro or Mexico City: Tequisquiapan is within an hour's drive of Querétaro city and about two hours from Mexico City.
logistics.lodging_strategy: The 2026 venue was still listed as TBD in Tequisquiapan in early November. Book in Tequisquiapan once it is named, or in Querétaro city an hour away.
logistics.food: Waffles and coffee open at 6:00 am on race day; Hammer Nutrition aid and hydration stations on course.
logistics.packet_pickup: 2026: Saturday, November 21, 10:00 am to 6:00 pm at the expo.

history.founder: Monuments of Cycling (Belgian Waffle Ride), with local organizer Siddhartha Camil
history.origin_story: BWR announced a Mexico round in January 2023 as its series finale, promising the largest prize purse of its seven races. The first edition ran November 25-26, 2023 from El Lobo Hacienda in El Marqués, Querétaro. The 2025 edition started at Bodegas Vaivén, and the 2026 edition is based in Tequisquiapan.
notable_moments: 2023: First edition from El Lobo Hacienda in El Marqués; Adam Roberge and Anet Barrera won the Waffle, and 22% of riders were women
2024: Well over 550 riders, billed as the largest gravel race in Mexican history
2025: Ulises Castillo beat Gerardo Ulloa by two seconds over 112 miles, with Ian Boswell third; Brenda Santoyo beat Anet Barrera by five seconds
2026: Based in Tequisquiapan with a 1,000-rider cap
2027: Fifth edition announced to close the BWR calendar; date not yet on the organizer's site
history.reputation: Billed as the largest gravel race in Mexico, and the last stop on the BWR calendar.

course_description.character: The Waffle is listed as +180 km from Tequisquiapan over fast gravel roads, technical sectors, vineyard country and ranch roads. Velo places the 2027 route among vineyards, ranch roads and historic towns with views of Peña de Bernal. No route file or climbing figure is published, and the distance moves: a 2023 finisher put that year's Waffle at 159 km.

logistics.explanation: Moderate planning. Tequisquiapan is within an hour's drive of Querétaro city and about two hours from Mexico City [11], and the 2026 venue was still listed as TBD in November [1].

length.explanation: Long, not ultra. The Waffle is listed as +180 km, about 112 miles [1][10]; the 2023 edition ran closer to 159 km [8].

technicality.explanation: Mixed. The organizer lists technical sectors alongside fast gravel and ranch roads, and keeps mountain bikes off the Waffle [1]. A 2023 finisher described technical climbs and descents [8].

elevation.explanation: Provisional. Nobody publishes a gain figure. The 2025 men's winner averaged about 36 km/h over 112 miles [10], which is not the speed of a mountain course. Mid-scale until a route file says otherwise.

climate.explanation: Mostly kind. 2025 ran in mild weather under clear skies [10]. The test is a 5:30 am rider call at 1,880 m [1][11] and a route that closes at 6:00 pm [1].

altitude.explanation: Real. Tequisquiapan sits at 1,880 m (6,170 ft) [11]. Riders from sea level will feel it by the second half of 180 km.

adventure.explanation: A proper destination. Vineyards, ranch roads, historic towns and views of Peña de Bernal [4], in Querétaro's wine-and-cheese country [11].

prestige.explanation: A series badge on a young race. It closes the BWR calendar [4][6] and is billed as the largest gravel race in Mexico [9], but three editions carry less weight than the US Waffles.

race_quality.explanation: Good, with gaps. The 2026 page publishes a full schedule, Hammer aid stations, Shimano neutral service, medical stations and sweep vans [1]. It publishes no route file, no climbing figure and no fixed cutoffs [1].

experience.explanation: A full weekend: Friday meet-and-greet, a Saturday expo with social rides and a beer garden, and waffles and coffee before the start [1]. Enjoyable; three editions in, not yet a legend.

community.explanation: Growing. 2024 drew well over 550 riders, with women above 22% of the field [9], matching the 22% at the first edition [7].

field_depth.explanation: Competitive at the front. Adam Roberge won the first edition [7]. In 2025 Ulises Castillo won by two seconds with Ian Boswell third, and Brenda Santoyo won the women's race by five seconds [10].

value.explanation: Good. 2026 Waffle entry runs from $99 early bird to $220 at the expo, plus 16% VAT, for 180 km with aid, neutral service, medical support and a $5,000 purse [1].

expenses.explanation: Moderate. Entry is modest [1]; for riders from outside Mexico, flights into Querétaro or Mexico City and wine-country lodging are most of the bill.
